messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

You will be given a piece of text and a list of relational triples in the format of [Subject, Relation, Object] extracted from the text. For each relation present in the triples, your task is to write a description to express the meaning of the relation.

Here are some examples:
Example 1:
Text: Lipitor (atorvastatin) belongs to a group of drugs called statins. Lipitor is used together with diet to lower blood levels of "bad" cholesterol (LDL) and to reduce the risk of stroke and heart attack.
Triples: [["Lipitor", "has generic name", "atorvastatin"], ["Lipitor", "belongs to drug class", "statins"], ["Lipitor", "treats", "high LDL cholesterol"], ["Lipitor", "reduces risk of", "stroke"]]
Relations: ["has generic name", "belongs to drug class", "treats", "reduces risk of"]
Answer:
has generic name: The subject drug is known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.
belongs to drug class: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.
reduces risk of: The subject drug is used to lower the risk of the medical event or condition specified by the object entity.

Example 2:
Text: You should not use metformin if you have severe kidney disease. Tell your doctor if you have ever had liver disease. Metformin may cause lactic acidosis, a serious condition. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking metformin.
Triples: [["metformin", "contraindicated in", "severe kidney disease"], ["metformin", "use with caution in", "liver disease"], ["metformin", "has serious side effect", "lactic acidosis"], ["metformin", "should be avoided with", "alcohol"]]
Relations: ["contraindicated in", "use with caution in", "has serious side effect", "should be avoided with"]
Answer:
contraindicated in: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
use with caution in: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
has serious side effect: The subject drug may cause the serious or dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity.
should be avoided with: Patients taking the subject drug should avoid the substance or activity specified by the object entity.

Example 3:
Text: Amlodipine is available as oral tablets in strengths of 2.5 mg, 5 mg, and 10 mg. Overdose symptoms may include rapid heartbeats and fainting. Norvasc is made by Pfizer.
Triples: [["amlodipine", "has dosage form", "oral tablet"], ["amlodipine", "has strength", "2.5 mg"], ["amlodipine", "has overdose symptom", "fainting"], ["Norvasc", "manufactured by", "Pfizer"]]
Relations: ["has dosage form", "has strength", "has overdose symptom", "manufactured by"]
Answer:
has dosage form: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
has strength: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
has overdose symptom: An overdose of the subject drug may cause the symptom specified by the object entity.
manufactured by: The subject drug is manufactured or marketed by the company specified by the object entity.

Now please write relation descriptions given the following text and triples. Note that the description needs to be general and can be used to describe relations between other entities as well. Pay attention to the order of subject and object entities. Write exactly one line per relation in the form "relation: description" and nothing else.
Text: Menstrual changes is not among the most commonly reported side effects.
Pregnancy - taking Fluoxetine in late pregnancy may increase the risk of certain complications in newborns.
Women who are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding should discuss the risks and benefits with their doctor.
These women should do this before continuing or starting this medicine.
Does fluoxetine (Prozac) help with anxiety?
:
Fluoxetine is not FDA-approved specifically for generalized anxiety disorder.
Fluoxetine is FDA-approved to treat panic disorder.
Panic disorder is a type of anxiety disorder.
Fluoxetine is also approved for obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD).
OCD has a significant anxiety component.
Fluoxetine is sometimes prescribed off-label by doctors for anxiety symptoms.
Fluoxetine is not FDA-approved for generalized anxiety disorder.
SSRIs are a well-established treatment class for anxiety conditions.
Off-label means the drug is being used in a way not specifically approved by the FDA.
It is supported by clinical evidence.
You may experience anxiety alongside depression.
Triples: [["Fluoxetine", "has side effect", "menstrual changes"], ["Fluoxetine", "has risk in", "late pregnancy"], ["Fluoxetine", "has risk in", "newborn complications"], ["Fluoxetine", "has administration instruction", "discuss risks and benefits with doctor"], ["Fluoxetine", "has administration instruction", "consult doctor before continuing or starting medicine"], ["Fluoxetine", "not fda approved for", "generalized anxiety disorder"], ["Fluoxetine", "fda approved to treat", "panic disorder"], ["panic disorder", "is type of", "anxiety disorder"], ["Fluoxetine", "fda approved to treat", "obsessive-compulsive disorder"], ["obsessive-compulsive disorder", "has component", "anxiety"], ["Fluoxetine", "sometimes prescribed off label for", "anxiety symptoms"], ["SSRIs", "are treatment class for", "anxiety conditions"], ["off-label", "means drug used in way", "not specifically approved by FDA"], ["off-label", "is supported by", "clinical evidence"], ["depression", "may be accompanied by", "anxiety"]]
Relations: ["are treatment class for", "fda approved to treat", "has administration instruction", "has component", "has risk in", "has side effect", "is supported by", "is type of", "may be accompanied by", "means drug used in way", "not fda approved for", "sometimes prescribed off label for"]
Answer:

completion:
are treatment class for: The subject entity is a pharmacological class that is used to treat the medical condition specified by the object entity.
fda approved to treat: The subject drug is officially approved by the FDA to treat the medical condition specified by the object entity.
has administration instruction: The subject drug requires the administration instruction specified by the object entity to be followed by patients.
has component: The subject condition or disorder includes or contains the component specified by the object entity.
has risk in: The subject drug may pose a risk or complication in the situation or group specified by the object entity.
has side effect: The subject drug may cause the adverse effect specified by the object entity.
is supported by: The subject concept or statement is supported or validated by the evidence or entity specified by the object entity.
is type of: The subject condition or entity is a specific type or subclass of the object entity.
may be accompanied by: The subject condition or entity may occur alongside or be associated with the condition specified by the object entity.
means drug used in way: The subject term or concept describes the usage of a drug in the manner specified by the object entity.
not fda approved for: The subject drug is not officially approved by the FDA to treat or manage the condition specified by the object entity.
sometimes prescribed off label for: The subject drug is occasionally prescribed by healthcare providers for the condition or symptom specified by the object entity, despite not being FDA-approved for it.
